record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Two-machine flow shop with proportional operations
record.original_question: Given a two-machine flow shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij t when it starts at time t, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this two-machine flow-shop time-dependent scheduling problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two-machine flow shop scheduling problem with time-dependent (proportional) processing times.

Setup:
- There are two machines M_1 and M_2 in series, and n jobs J_1, ..., J_n.
- Each job J_j consists of two operations: operation 1 must be processed on M_1 and operation 2 must be processed on M_2; operation 2 of J_j can start only after operation 1 of J_j has completed.
- Each machine processes at most one operation at a time, and preemption is not allowed.
- The processing time of operation i of job j (i ∈ {1,2}, j ∈ {1,...,n}) is proportional and time-dependent: if this operation starts at time t ≥ 0, then its processing time is p_{ij}(t) = b_{ij} · t, where b_{ij} > 0 is a given deterioration rate. (Equivalently, an operation started at time t finishes at time t(1+b_{ij}).)
- A common starting time t_0 > 0 is given for the schedule.
- Let C_j denote the completion time of job J_j (i.e., the completion time of its operation on M_2).

Objective: Find a schedule (a permutation of jobs and start times for each operation) that minimizes the total completion time Σ_{j=1}^n C_j.

Question: Determine the computational complexity of this problem. Specifically, is it NP-hard (at least in the ordinary sense), or does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm solving it to optimality?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work on two-machine flow shop scheduling with deteriorating/proportional processing times (branch-and-bound algorithms, dominance properties, and polynomial-time results under additional structural assumptions), but did not surface a definitive complexity classification (NP-hardness proof or polynomial algorithm) for the exact problem F2 | p_{ij} = b_{ij} t | ΣC_j. The status appears to remain unresolved in the publicly indexed literature.

status_evidence.title: Solution algorithms for the total weighted completion time minimization flow shop scheduling with decreasing linear deterioration
status_evidence.snippet: Branch-and-bound and heuristic algorithms for total weighted completion time in flow shop with linear deterioration, indicating the problem is treated as computationally hard with no known polynomial algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: Related two-machine flow shop deteriorating-jobs problems with sum-of-completion-times objectives are tackled by branch-and-bound rather than polynomial algorithms, consistent with the complexity being open or hard.

status_evidence.title: Minimizing total completion time in a two-machine flowshop with a learning effect
status_evidence.snippet: Studies F2||ΣC_j variants under time-dependent/learning effects without giving a polynomial algorithm in the general proportional case.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related variants of F2 with time-dependent processing times do not have published polynomial algorithms for ΣC_j in the general proportional case.
